title: Observed North Pacific pressure did not remove the 2020-2025 PDO mean gap in a model fitted to 1951-2019
abstract: We tested whether observed North Pacific pressure accounts for the 2020-2025 PDO mean after lagged ENSO and PDO memory are allowed for. Models fitted to 1951-2019 used current pressure and two pressure lags. The observed mean was -1.995. The pressure model gave a simulated mean of -0.788 and a central 95% conditional model range of -1.431 to -0.213. None of 1,999 draws was as low as the observation. Planned block, memory, season and training-period checks did not remove the gap. Pressure cut monthly reconstruction mean squared error by 23.76% in a separate 1980-2019 test, with a conditional 95% interval of 17.77% to 28.81%. Yet its long-mean ranges missed two of six earlier means. Thus useful monthly information did not validate the model for sustained departures. This extends prior campaign pressure and PNA tests on overlapping data. It is not a causal test or a calibrated climate tail probability. A selected interval, revised indices, incomplete slow memory and bootstrap assumptions limit inference. Code, exact source hashes, retrieval instructions, aggregate evidence, simulation draws, a figure and numerical checks are included. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Conditional ranges for recent six-year PDO means and earlier window checks. These are model ranges, not calibrated climate probabilities.
